miniMessageTheme.source:
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Theme
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# This file defines named colors, called "tokens", that locale files use
# through the <t:token> tag (chat messages, GUI menus, Bedrock forms and
# dialogs).
#
# Example: a locale entry "<t:error>You can't do this." renders with the style
# configured at theme.tokens.error below. Changing that one value re-colors
# every message that uses the <t:error> tag - without touching the locale
# files.
#
# Accepted values: MiniMessage color and decoration tags, e.g.:
#   - a color alone: "<red>", "<#ff8080>"
#   - color plus decorations: "<b><white>", "<red><st>"
# Only color and decoration tags are allowed (no click/hover/gradients) - a
# token is a style definition, not a message.
#
# A value left empty (e.g. entity_land: "") disables that token: <t:entity_land>
# still resolves, it just applies no styling at all, instead of failing as an
# unknown token. Useful for turning a token off without hunting down and
# removing every place it's used across the locale files.
#
# This file is self-contained and can be copied between servers to share a
# theme.
theme:

  # Tokens used by the default locale files. You can change their styles, but
  # they cannot be removed - locale entries reference them by name.
  #
  # Grouped below by role rather than alphabetically: body-text tones, then
  # the "value" tokens that highlight something embedded in that tone's prose
  # (a name, a number, a cost, a limit, a duration, a command - all serve the
  # same purpose of standing out against the surrounding text), then
  # headings, then everything else.
  tokens:

    # --- Body/prose tones ---

    # Regular message and lore text.
    regular: "<gray>"

    # Positive feedback: success messages, "Yes", enabled states.
    success: "<green>"

    # Failure and error message text.
    error: "<red>"

    # Positive connotation inline within otherwise-neutral text: a
    # beneficial effect, a favorable relation, a gain - distinct from
    # success, which is reserved for "this action succeeded" messages.
    positive: "<green>"

    # Negative connotation inline within otherwise-neutral text: a harmful
    # effect, a hostile relation, a loss - distinct from error, which is
    # reserved for "this action failed" messages.
    negative: "<red>"

    # --- Embedded-value tokens ---
    # Each highlights a value quoted inside its matching prose tone above
    # (or, for cost/limit/time/cmd, a specific value type regardless of tone).

    # Values inside regular text that players look for: numbers, owners,
    # page counts.
    regular_value: "<yellow>"

    # Values inside success messages, such as names. Brighter than the
    # surrounding success text so the important part stands out.
    success_value: "<#80ff80>"

    # Values inside error messages, such as names. Brighter than the
    # surrounding error text so the important part stands out.
    error_value: "<#ff8080>"

    # Values with positive connotation, such as a beneficial stat or a gain.
    positive_value: "<#80ff80>"

    # Values with negative connotation, such as a harmful stat or a loss.
    negative_value: "<#ff8080>"

    # Prices and costs: {cost}/{costs} placeholders. Distinct from
    # regular_value so money always reads the same regardless of surrounding
    # text color.
    cost: "<red>"

    # Limits and thresholds: min/max values (e.g. {max} chunks, {min}
    # balance). Distinct from cost since a limit isn't money, and from
    # regular_value so it stays recognizable wherever it's quoted, including
    # inside otherwise-neutral text.
    limit: "<yellow>"

    # Durations and timestamps.
    time: "<yellow>"

    # Commands, command arguments and click-to-run hints.
    cmd: "<yellow>"

    # --- Headings ---

    # Titles and headings: title messages and GUI item names.
    regular_heading: "<b><gold>"

    # Headings of success states, e.g. GUI item names like "Request Accepted".
    success_heading: "<b><dark_green>"

    # Headings of error states, e.g. GUI item names like "Not allowed" or
    # "Missing Permission".
    error_heading: "<b><dark_red>"

    # Headings with positive connotation, e.g. GUI item names for a
    # beneficial effect or a favorable relation.
    positive_heading: "<b><dark_green>"

    # Headings with negative connotation, e.g. GUI item names for a harmful
    # effect or a hostile relation.
    negative_heading: "<b><dark_red>"

    # Headings of repeating list-row items (GUI menu entries prefixed
    # "entry_", e.g. a land/nation row, an invite, a flag toggle) - kept
    # distinct from regular_heading so list rows can be recolored without
    # affecting single-purpose menu item names.
    entry_heading: "<gold>"

    # --- Structural ---

    # Decorations around text: brackets, bullets, separators and dashes.
    decoration: "<dark_gray>"

    # --- Surface-specific ---

    # Java Edition inventory menu titles, rendered on the light inventory
    # background - needs a dark color, unlike tooltip text.
    menu_title: "<dark_gray>"

    # GUI-menu-only: keybind hints in item lore (LEFT CLICK, RIGHT CLICK,
    # SHIFT + ... variants, DROP). Never used in chat/Bedrock/dialog text.
    click: "<aqua>"

    # --- Other ---

    # The plugin brand color, used by the chat prefix.
    prefix: "<dark_green>"

    # Content written or supplied by players: chat messages, land descriptions,
    # inbox posts, stored items.
    user_content: "<white>"

    # --- Entity identity ---
    # Each entity type keeps a recognizable color across all menus and messages.

    entity_land: "<dark_green>"
    entity_nation: "<blue>"

  # Your own tokens. Every entry added here becomes available as a tag in all
  # locale files. For example, adding
  #   highlight: "<#00e617>"
  # makes <t:highlight> usable in any message or menu text.
  # This section is never modified by plugin updates.
  custom: {}

  # Optional per-surface overrides. Java Edition menus (item tooltips,
  # inventory titles and dialogs) use these values for the listed tokens;
  # anything not listed falls back to the sections above. Example:
  #   regular: "<white>"
  # This section is never modified by plugin updates.
  gui:
    regular: "<white>"

  # Optional per-surface overrides for dialogs, which render on dark panels
  # similar to Bedrock forms. Anything not listed falls back to the sections
  # above.
  # This section is never modified by plugin updates.
  dialog:
    regular: "<white>"

  # Optional per-surface overrides for Bedrock Edition forms. Anything not
  # listed falls back to the sections above.
  # This section is never modified by plugin updates.
  bedrock:
    # Bedrock forms render text on dark panels: brighter body text reads better there.
    regular: "<white>"
    # Headings label form buttons and the light title strip. Bedrock forms only
    # support the 16 legacy colors - NOT hex (an <#rrggbb> renders black there) -
    # and there is no "dark gold" among them, so the neutral headings use black
    # for maximum contrast on the light-gray buttons instead of the washed-out
    # bright gold, while the semantic ones stay dark_green/dark_red. (Swap
    # regular_heading/entry_heading to <dark_gray> or <gold> to taste.)
    regular_heading: "<black>"
    entry_heading: "<black>"
    success_heading: "<dark_green>"
    error_heading: "<dark_red>"
    positive_heading: "<dark_green>"
    negative_heading: "<dark_red>"
